title: Control 1  |  User shall not spend more than $50,000 per year.
question: Display the name and total amount spent during the year for all employees who spent more than $50,000 in 2014. Sort by the total amount spent with the larger amounts listed first.
sql:
SELECT
    FullName,
    ROUND(SUM(Amount), 2) AS TotalAmount
FROM pcards
WHERE Year = 2014
  AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
GROUP BY FullName
HAVING SUM(Amount) > 50000
ORDER BY TotalAmount DESC

title: Control 2  |  User shall not spend more than $10,000 per month without approval.
question: Display the name, total amount spent during the month and the month for all employees who spent more than $10,000 per month in 2014. Sort by month (January listed first) and then total the amount spent with the larger amounts listed first.
sql:
SELECT
    FullName,
    Month,
    ROUND(SUM(Amount), 2) AS TotalAmount
FROM pcards
WHERE Year = 2014
  AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
GROUP BY FullName, Month
HAVING SUM(Amount) > 10000
ORDER BY Month ASC, TotalAmount DESC

title: Control 3  |  User shall not spend more than $5,000 per transaction.
question: Display all transaction details (Amount, Name, Description, Vendor, TransactionDate, PostedDate and MCC) for any transaction in 2014 that was for more than $5,000. Sort by the total transaction amount.
sql:
SELECT
    Amount,
    FullName AS Name,
    Description,
    Vendor,
    TransactionDate,
    PostedDate,
    MCC
FROM pcards
WHERE Year = 2014
  AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND Amount > 5000
ORDER BY Amount ASC

title: Control 4  |  An amount more than $5,000 should not be split between two or more swipes of the card by the same person.
question: Display all transaction details where the vendor and purchaser are the same on a specific day, there is more than one transaction for the day and the combined total of the transaction was more than $5,000. Sort them in ascending order by the TransactionDate.
sql:
SELECT p.*
FROM pcards AS p
JOIN (
    SELECT FullName, Vendor, TransactionDate
    FROM pcards
    WHERE Year = 2014
      AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
      AND Amount > 0
    GROUP BY FullName, Vendor, TransactionDate
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
       AND SUM(Amount) > 5000
) AS g
  ON p.FullName = g.FullName
 AND p.Vendor = g.Vendor
 AND p.TransactionDate = g.TransactionDate
WHERE p.Year = 2014
  AND p.AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND p.Amount > 0
ORDER BY pcard_datetime(p.TransactionDate) ASC

title: Control 5  |  Purchases should not be split between two or more cardholders.
question: To simplify, we only will consider splitting these between two people. Display all transaction information in which the combined total for a vendor on a day was more than $5,000 and there were two different cardholders who made a purchase from that vendor (make sure the query excludes people who may have made double payments). Sort them in ascending order by the TransactionDate.
sql:
SELECT p.*
FROM pcards AS p
JOIN (
    SELECT
        Vendor,
        TransactionDate
    FROM pcards
    WHERE Year = 2014
      AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
      AND Amount > 0
    GROUP BY Vendor, TransactionDate
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 2
       AND COUNT(DISTINCT FullName) = 2
       AND SUM(Amount) > 5000
) AS g
  ON p.Vendor = g.Vendor
 AND p.TransactionDate = g.TransactionDate
WHERE p.Year = 2014
  AND p.AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND p.Amount > 0
ORDER BY pcard_datetime(p.TransactionDate) ASC

title: Control 6  |  Purchases should not be split between two or more vendors.
question: To simplify, we will only consider splitting these between two vendors. Display all transaction information in which the combined total for a person on a day was more than $5,000 and there were purchases made at two different vendors (make sure the query excludes people who may have made double payments at one vendor). Sort them in ascending order by the TransactionDate.
sql:
SELECT p.*
FROM pcards AS p
JOIN (
    SELECT
        FullName,
        TransactionDate
    FROM pcards
    WHERE Year = 2014
      AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
      AND Amount > 0
    GROUP BY FullName, TransactionDate
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 2
       AND COUNT(DISTINCT Vendor) = 2
       AND SUM(Amount) > 5000
) AS g
  ON p.FullName = g.FullName
 AND p.TransactionDate = g.TransactionDate
WHERE p.Year = 2014
  AND p.AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND p.Amount > 0
ORDER BY pcard_datetime(p.TransactionDate) ASC

title: Control 7  |  Transactions are prohibited for expenses for food and mileage while traveling. A per diem for food expenses and mileage may be claimed using a travel voucher.
question: For the days when an employee makes a purchase using an MCC that contains the words hotel, motel, resort or inn, return all transaction details about any transactions for those employees who on those days also contain MCCs that have the words food or restaurant. Sort them in ascending order by name and then the amount.
sql:
SELECT p.*
FROM pcards AS p
WHERE p.Year = 2014
  AND p.AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND (
       LOWER(p.MCC) LIKE '%food%'
       OR LOWER(p.MCC) LIKE '%restaurant%'
  )
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM pcards AS h
      WHERE h.Year = 2014
        AND h.AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
        AND h.FullName = p.FullName
        AND h.TransactionDate = p.TransactionDate
        AND (
             LOWER(h.MCC) LIKE '%hotel%'
             OR LOWER(h.MCC) LIKE '%motel%'
             OR LOWER(h.MCC) LIKE '%resort%'
             OR LOWER(h.MCC) LIKE '%inn%'
        )
  )
ORDER BY p.FullName ASC, p.Amount ASC

title: Question 1  |  Benford's analysis of first digits
question: Using OSU transactions from calendar year 2014, conduct a Benford's analysis of the first digit of transaction amounts. Exclude amounts below $1.00. The final output must be a single query showing the percentage of transactions beginning with each digit from 1 through 9, with percentages rounded to three decimal places. Use the results to assess whether the data indicate a relatively low or high fraud risk.
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE digits(d) AS (
    VALUES(1)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT d + 1
    FROM digits
    WHERE d < 9
),
first_digits AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(Amount AS TEXT), 1, 1) AS INTEGER) AS FirstDigit
    FROM pcards
    WHERE Year = 2014
      AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
      AND Amount >= 1.00
)
SELECT
    d AS FirstDigit,
    ROUND(
        100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN FirstDigit = d THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
        / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM first_digits),
        3
    ) AS Percentage
FROM digits
LEFT JOIN first_digits
    ON FirstDigit = d
GROUP BY d
ORDER BY d

title: Question 2  |  Potential duplicate transactions
question: Identify possible duplicate payments in the OSU 2014 data. Treat positive charges as possible duplicates when they have the same transaction date, vendor, cardholder first initial, cardholder last name and amount; if more than two charges match, include all matching charges. Exclude returns. Return TransactionDate, Vendor, FullName and Amount, and sort in ascending order by TransactionDate and then Vendor.
sql:
WITH DuplicateGroups AS (
    SELECT
        TransactionDate,
        Vendor,
        CardholderFirstInitial,
        CardholderLastName,
        Amount
    FROM pcards
    WHERE Year = 2014
      AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
      AND Amount > 0
    GROUP BY
        TransactionDate,
        Vendor,
        CardholderFirstInitial,
        CardholderLastName,
        Amount
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
)
SELECT
    p.TransactionDate,
    p.Vendor,
    p.FullName,
    p.Amount
FROM pcards AS p
JOIN DuplicateGroups AS d
  ON p.TransactionDate = d.TransactionDate
 AND p.Vendor = d.Vendor
 AND p.CardholderFirstInitial = d.CardholderFirstInitial
 AND p.CardholderLastName = d.CardholderLastName
 AND p.Amount = d.Amount
WHERE p.Year = 2014
  AND p.AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND p.Amount > 0
ORDER BY
    pcard_datetime(p.TransactionDate),
    p.Vendor,
    p.FullName,
    p.Amount

title: Question 3  |  Employees repeatedly associated with possible duplicates
question: Using the possible duplicate population from Question 2, list each employee and the number of separate occasions on which the employee has a possible duplicate transaction. Count duplicate occasions rather than the number of transaction rows, and sort with the largest number of occasions first so the highest-risk employees can be investigated.
sql:
WITH DuplicateGroups AS (
    SELECT
        CardholderFirstInitial,
        CardholderLastName,
        FullName,
        TransactionDate,
        Vendor,
        Amount
    FROM pcards
    WHERE Year = 2014
      AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
      AND Amount > 0
    GROUP BY
        CardholderFirstInitial,
        CardholderLastName,
        FullName,
        TransactionDate,
        Vendor,
        Amount
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
)
SELECT
    FullName,
    COUNT(*) AS DuplicateOccasions
FROM DuplicateGroups
GROUP BY FullName
ORDER BY
    DuplicateOccasions DESC,
    FullName ASC

title: Question 4  |  Four-digit round-number transactions
question: Return all positive OSU transactions from 2014 with four-digit whole-dollar amounts that end in 000, ignoring cents. Include Amount, Vendor, Description and FullName. Sort in ascending order by Vendor and then FullName to identify patterns.
sql:
SELECT
    Amount,
    Vendor,
    Description,
    FullName
FROM pcards
WHERE Year = 2014
  AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND Amount >= 1000
  AND Amount < 10000
  AND Amount = CAST(Amount AS INTEGER)
  AND CAST(Amount AS INTEGER) % 1000 = 0
ORDER BY
    Vendor ASC,
    FullName ASC

title: Question 5  |  Student-defined fraud test
question: Identify positive 2014 OSU transactions from $4,900 through $5,000, inclusive, as a screen for purchases concentrated near the single-purchase limit. Return FullName, Amount, Vendor, TransactionDate, Description and MCC; sort by Amount descending and FullName ascending. The narrow range focuses follow-up, but purchases at or below the limit are not inherently improper.
sql:
SELECT
    FullName,
    Amount,
    Vendor,
    TransactionDate,
    Description,
    MCC
FROM pcards
WHERE Year = 2014
  AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND Amount > 0
  AND Amount >= 4900
  AND Amount <= 5000
ORDER BY
    Amount DESC,
    FullName ASC

title: Question 6  |  Student-defined fraud test
question: Identify employee-vendor-amount combinations with at least three positive transactions in 2014. Return FullName, Vendor, Amount and TransactionCount; sort by count descending, then employee and vendor ascending. Requiring three occurrences reduces isolated matches. Unlike Question 2, this test does not require the same date and can identify recurring fixed-price charges.
sql:
SELECT
    FullName,
    Vendor,
    Amount,
    COUNT(*) AS TransactionCount
FROM pcards
WHERE Year = 2014
  AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND Amount > 0
GROUP BY
    FullName,
    Vendor,
    Amount
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY
    TransactionCount DESC,
    FullName ASC,
    Vendor ASC

title: Question 7  |  Student-defined fraud test
question: Identify employee-vendor relationships involving at least 20 positive transactions in 2014, regardless of amount. Return FullName, Vendor, TransactionCount and TotalAmount; sort by count descending and total amount descending. The threshold focuses on sustained purchasing relationships; frequency must be assessed in light of the employee’s role and purchasing needs.
sql:
SELECT
    FullName,
    Vendor,
    COUNT(*) AS TransactionCount,
    ROUND(SUM(Amount), 2) AS TotalAmount
FROM pcards
WHERE Year = 2014
  AND AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND Amount > 0
GROUP BY
    FullName,
    Vendor
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY
    TransactionCount DESC,
    TotalAmount DESC

title: Question 8  |  Student-defined fraud test
question: Identify negative 2014 OSU transactions for which the same employee and vendor have no positive transaction of the exact opposite amount in the 2014 OSU data. Return FullName, Vendor, Amount, TransactionDate, Description and MCC, ordered by absolute Amount descending. Matching both employee and vendor makes the screen more specific, but does not resolve partial credits or purchases outside the year.
sql:
SELECT
    n.FullName,
    n.Vendor,
    n.Amount,
    n.TransactionDate,
    n.Description,
    n.MCC
FROM pcards AS n
WHERE n.Year = 2014
  AND n.AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
  AND n.Amount < 0
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM pcards AS p
      WHERE p.Year = 2014
        AND p.AgencyName = 'OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY'
        AND p.FullName = n.FullName
        AND p.Vendor = n.Vendor
        AND p.Amount = -n.Amount
        AND p.Amount > 0
  )
ORDER BY ABS(n.Amount) DESC
